## CONGO, REPUBLIC OF — profile (page 147)

- Header facts: Sub-Saharan Africa; Lower-middle-income; Blend; Data as reported (A); Population 6.5 million; GNI 14,601; unit line: US$ million, unless otherwise indicated.
- Total external debt stock, 2025: 7,711, with +9.9% from 2024.

- Figure 1 Total external debt, 2015–25:
  - Printed start/end values: 6,766 (2015) and 7,711 (2025).
  - Line shape: debt is roughly flat to slightly lower at first, rises by ≈2017, dips at ≈2018, then climbs sharply to a peak around ≈2019. It eases slightly around ≈2020–21, falls further through ≈2022–24, and rebounds in 2025.

- Figure 2 External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations:
  - Total external debt: 7,711
    - Public & publicly guaranteed: 7,187
    - Private nonguaranteed: 7
    - Short-term: 516
  - Public & publicly guaranteed — by creditor type: 7,187
    - Multilateral: 2,490
    - Bilateral: 2,210
    - Private creditors: 2,487
  - Multilateral: 2,490
    - World Bank-IDA: 707
    - AfDB: 539
    - Other multilateral: 1,244
  - Bilateral: 2,210
    - China: 1,561
    - France: 240
    - Other bilateral: 410

- Figure 3 Debt ratios, 2015–25:
  - External debt / exports: 108%, +22.7%; trend rises early, has no data values in 2017–18, then falls to the early 2020s before edging up by 2025.
  - External debt / GNI: 53%, +6.7%; trend rises to peaks around the late 2010s/early 2020s, then declines somewhat and ticks up at the end.
  - Debt service / exports: 7%, -46.2%; trend is low overall, with fluctuations and a decline to 2025.
  - Debt service / GNI: 4%, -53.2%; trend is fairly flat at first, rises to a peak around ≈2023, stays elevated around ≈2024, then drops sharply in 2025.

- Figure 4 Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025:
  - Official creditors:
    - Maturity: 28 yrs
    - Grace period: 4 yrs
    - Interest rate: 1.1%
  - Private creditors:
    - Maturity: 7 yrs
    - Grace period: 3 yrs
    - Interest rate: 9.9%

- Notes: Note: Figure 3 shows no data values for the exports-based ratios in 2017–18.
- Source: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
